method.summary: Tasks, fixtures, rubrics and answer keys written from skill.json + README.md only, then frozen (sha256 in FREEZE.txt) before any run. Each run: headless `claude -p` (Claude Code 2.1.303), model sonnet (claude-sonnet-5-5), cwd = fresh mkdtemp dir with the fixture copied in, tools limited to Skill,Read,Glob,Grep(,Edit,Write for MCP Mechanic), --setting-sources project, --strict-mcp-config with no servers, --no-session-persistence. Baseline: no skill. Skill: skills/<slug>/ minus evals/ copied to <tmp>/.claude/skills/<slug>/. Same prompt both conditions, 3 repeats per task per condition, interleaved order. No Bash, no web, no MCP.
method.permissions: Run in --permission-mode bypassPermissions with deny rules on Edit/Write under /Users, ~, /Library, /Applications, /etc, /opt, /usr, /Volumes, /private/tmp, /private/etc and on Read under /Users and ~. Reason: under acceptEdits, headless Claude Code refuses writes to .mcp.json as a protected config file, which would have failed every MCP file task for reasons unrelated to the skill (found in aborted attempt 1, archived under independent-runs/2026-10-21/aborted-attempt-1/). Outside-dir write attempts are also detected from the tool-call stream.
method.grading: Deterministic checks in web/scripts/eval-independent.ts (JSON parse, structure, secret strings, file locations, tool-call targets). Judgement items by a separate blind grader: `claude -p --model opus --tools ""`, one answer at a time, condition label removed, skill names and the word 'skill' redacted, order shuffled by a seeded hash. Grader prompts and raw outputs are in independent-runs/2026-10-21/grader/<blindId>.json; blind-mapping.json maps ids to runs.
method.agentRuns: 54 scored runs. Aborted attempt 1 used about 13 further agent invocations (7 completed, 6 killed); none are scored. Total agent invocations about 67, a little over the ~60 budget, plus 54 grader calls.

keyFindings: Skill invoked in 12/12 skill runs; 0 in baseline.
Planted-flaw recall was 1.0 in BOTH conditions (17 planted flaws x 3 repeats each). The planted flaws were too obvious to separate the conditions; recall does not show a skill benefit.
False positives (claims contradicting the design text): 0 in both conditions, as judged by the blind grader.
Output format: findings table with blocker/major/minor in 12/12 skill runs, 0/12 baseline runs (the README's promised format).
Severity calibration on planted flaws (given severity >= key minimum): skill 1.0, baseline 0.9 (baseline sometimes left items unrated or rated hardcoded key / LLM-to-customer as minor).

Clean blueprint B4: baseline answers framed 6 items as 'fix before building' (mapped to blocker; grader judged 5 of 6 not defensible) plus 5 majors; skill gave 0 blockers but 9 majors, and the grader judged none of the 9 needed major. The skill avoids blocker inflation but still over-rates on a clean design.
Both conditions rate most planted flaws as blocker, so severity is not very discriminating in either.
limitations: One agent model (sonnet), 3 repeats per blueprint per condition.
Recall hit the ceiling for both conditions: the planted flaws were textbook and well within the base model's reach, so this test cannot show whether the skill finds subtler flaws.
Blueprints are synthetic and written by the evaluator.

Baseline answers do not use blocker/major/minor; the grader mapped their labels ('Critical', 'fix before building', etc.) onto that scale, so baseline severity numbers, especially B4 blockers, depend on that mapping.
False positives and defensibility are judged by a same-vendor model (opus); the grader found zero false positives everywhere, which may be lenient.
comparisonWithAuthors: Authors' results-2026-10-21.json: 3 tasks x 3 repeats, regex checks written by the author: baseline 0.889 vs skill 1.0. This independent run does not reproduce a recall gap: both conditions found every planted flaw. The measurable differences here are format (table with severities) and somewhat better severity calibration, with fewer blocker-level false alarms on the clean design but more majors.
